Day Events Example

An event database organized by day: one gxDatabase file per YYYY/MM/DD folder, and a time-range query across days.

Source

What It Shows

Events that are only ever looked at by time (a trade log, readings, alerts, news) fit well in one database file per day:

day_events/2026/11/09/events.gxd
day_events/2026/11/10/events.gxd
...

Every file stays small, only today's file is written, and old days can be backed up, copied or deleted one folder at a time. The program:

  1. Appends fixed-size events (a UTC time stamp, a type, a ticker and a short text) to their day's file, creating the folders the first time a day is written. Events arrive in time order, so each day file is already sorted.
  2. Queries a range that starts inside one day and ends inside a later one. It opens only the days in the range, skips a day with no file and stops reading a day once it passes the end time.
  3. Checks the result against the same filter run over the events it wrote.

For lookups by key, add a gxBtree index next to each day's data file.

Running It

day_events [folder]            # default ./day_events, removed and rebuilt each run

Sample Output

Appended 48 events into day folders under day_events:

  day_events/2026/11/10/events.gxd

  day_events/2026/11/13/events.gxd
Query 2026-11-10 16:00 to 2026-11-13 15:00 UTC: 23 events from 3 day files (Nov 12 has none)
  2026-11-10 16:05:00  news  BTCS  event 5 of Nov 10
  ...
The query matches the events written
